newsitem.title: GERMANY: Bunds seen under pressure from weak dmk, U.S. mkt.
newsitem.headline: Bunds seen under pressure from weak dmk, U.S. mkt.

text.p: Bunds were little changed in early trade on Monday but dealers said the outlook was dimmed by Friday's sharp drop in U.S. bonds and the fear that the firm dollar will prompt the Bundesbank to raise its repo rate.
September Bund futures were quoted down five basis points at 102.30 at 0745 GMT and predicted they would move in a range of roughly 102.15 to 102.50.
Dealers said they were waiting for the release of German industrial output data for June which analysts expect to have risen 1.5 percent month-on-month after a fall of 0.2 percent in May.
The year-on-year growth rate is expected to slow down to 1.9 percent from 3.0 percent.
"The drop in U.S. bonds, the strong dollar, the lack of investor interest are all affecting the market, there's absolute nervousness around."

Dealers said the short end of the market was coming under pressure from speculation that the Bundesbank may switch to variable-rate repo tenders to pave the way for higher short-term rates to halt the mark's slide against the dollar.
The dollar was trading at 1.8624 marks, a third of a pfennig off its seven-and-a-half year high.

IBJ Research in Frankfurt wrote in a note to investors that Bundesbank action was imminent and that the most likely move was to choose a new repo policy -- a switch from the current three percent fixed-rate repo tender to a "double-decker" system from August 13.
"A two-week repo with a variable would be accompanied by another one for four weeks with a fixed rate of 3.1 percent," IBJ said.
"Thereby the bidding risk for the variable-rate repo will be capped at 3.1 percent and this combination would not require other European central banks to follow suit."
The Bundesbank has its first chance to act at 0700 GMT when makes its formal tender announcement for this week's repo allocation.
While this week's repo has already been fixed at 3.00 percent, analysts say the Bundesbank may make an additional announcement about next week's tender.
